quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as you can.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain balance. Steer toward the direction of the skid to get control back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see ahead clearly.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It can be dangerous. Instead, slow down and let them cross safely.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle in your right mirror.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into your original lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving.

questions.question: When driving past parked cars, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked cars to make room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out suddenly or a parked car may start moving without seeing you.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross.
When the crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross.
questions.explanation: Always expect a train on any track at any time. Make sure your entire vehicle clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must give you the right-of-way.
You must give them the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use white canes or guide dogs. You must let them cross safely.

questions.question: When must you use low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this warning sign mean?

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells drivers that the road is getting narrower. Move to the left lane.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means do not pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beams. If fog is too thick to see, pull over and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way.
There is a detour to the right for road construction.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn at an extreme angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells drivers to slow down for a sharp turn ahead.

questions.question: When a school bus has red lights flashing, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students get off the bus.
The stop arm goes up.
The stop arm goes up and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm goes up and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm goes up, and the bus moves.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. Before you turn, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are near a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children near schools.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, and you could cause a crash.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive if you can walk in a straight line after drinking.
Your driving is not impaired if you are below the legal alcohol limit.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is necessary to respond safely to things you see or hear while driving. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Watch traffic in front of you and next to you.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
Only the right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the car ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes in your direction.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check traffic, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Both directions can pass.
Only the side with the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the side with the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When there is a dashed yellow line on one side and a solid yellow line on the other, only traffic next to the dashed line can cross to pass. Traffic next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: After passing a car, when do you have enough space to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move back.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
When you see both of the passed car's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see both of the passed car's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane, make sure there is a safe distance between you and the other car. When you can see both headlights in your mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic to back up and should be avoided.

questions.question: Is backing up dangerous?

options.text: Yes, it is always dangerous.
It is dangerous only if you have a helper.
It is only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see behind your vehicle. Be extra careful when backing up.

questions.question: The car ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What do you do?

options.text: Pass it slowly at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: You have a minor crash with no injuries or major damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
Do not move your vehicle at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries or deaths, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who:

options.text: Are on your left.
Arrived before you.
Are across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, let drivers go in the order they arrived. If drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
